courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: Now of course here in this form, we can also show error messages when the input is invalid.
Now I'll not do it here for the title but I'll do it for the description because there, it might be unclear
that one possible error source is that it's too long.
So here, I'll add an ion-row and in that ion-row, I'll add an ion-column and that column will of course receive
the same sizing as the column which holds the actual input
and then here, I'll add a paragraph where I say description must not be longer than 180 characters, like that
and I want to show that row only if our description input is invalid and has been touched.
Now how do we get access to that? Previously in the template-driven approach,
we added a local reference to the control and assigned it to ngModel.
Well here in the reactive approach, we already do have access to the entire form here on this form property
and therefore in our template
here in ngIf, I can just reach out to form and now to get access to a specific control, there is a get
method to which I pass the name of that control which here is description and then there, I can access
valid and so on.
So here, I can access valid and check if it's not valid,
now of course I also want to make sure that the user had a chance to interact with the input and
therefore I'll also check if form get description touched is true. And now we can save that to see
whether that works, as this reloads,
no error here but if I type in here and I click out of that, now I see the error. Of course, I also see
the error because I didn't enter anything here and therefore maybe we should sharpen this message and we
say description must be between 1 and 180 characters and this should be clearer. Now if i save this again,
we should have a better user experience because we show a useful message here
if this is invalid. Now let's also try breaking that 180 characters
case here by just entering a lot of characters here and that looks good.
I did lose focus and still it's invalid, if I clear this however and enter a shorter text,
this works.
Now of course, you can add more error messages, for example also to the price if you want to or
to the dates
but I'll leave it like this and instead, I want to have a look at this button.
Of course, this button should only be pressable when this form is valid and otherwise, it should be disabled.
Now this can be implemented in a relatively easy way because we have access to our form property here,
we can go up to that button and there, I will simply set the disabled attribute again and I'll disable
this if form valid is false,
so if the form is not valid and that's all. I don't care about anything else, I can just check if the
entire form is valid or not
and I do disable the button if it's not. And therefore now, this button is disabled as you can see
but if I enter something here and here and I do choose valid dates here,
now as I lose focus on the last date, this becomes active. That's the new offer form,
obviously I'm not doing anything with the data we gather here, we'll add this over the next lectures, that
we actually store this and later also centers to a server but being able to fetch the data is already
a great first step.
Now what about editing places though?
We got these places here, we got this edit button, we got the edit offer page but on that page, we're
not doing anything. So let's make sure that there, we also load data about the place we selected here
and that were then able to edit it.
